n: In God’s right hand is a scroll written on both sides and sealed with seven seals. Latter-day Saint revelation explains it contains God’s will and works for the earth’s seven thousand years of temporal existence.

f.w: written within and on the backside

n: A mighty angel calls out: who is worthy to break the seals and open the scroll?
No one anywhere—in heaven, on earth, or in the world of the dead—could open it or even look inside.
John wept bitterly, because if no one could open the scroll, God’s plan for the world seemed stalled.
An elder comforts him: the Lion of Judah, the Root of David, has triumphed and can open the scroll. These are royal titles for the Messiah.

f.w: Lion of the tribe of Juda

n: John turns to see the Lion—and sees a Lamb that looks slaughtered. Christ conquers through His sacrifice. The JST describes twelve horns and twelve eyes, representing the twelve servants of God.

f.w: Lamb as it had been slain

n: The Lamb steps forward and takes the scroll from the right hand of the One on the throne. Only Christ can carry out the Father’s plan.
The creatures and elders fall before the Lamb with harps and golden bowls of incense, which represent the prayers of the Saints. Our prayers are precious in heaven.
They sing a new song: the Lamb is worthy because He was slain and, by His blood, redeemed people from every family, language, people, and nation.

f.w: redeemed us to God by thy blood

n: He has made them kings and priests to God, and they will reign on the earth—a hint of the coming Millennium.
John hears countless angels—“ten thousand times ten thousand”—surrounding the throne.
They proclaim loudly that the slain Lamb is worthy of seven honors: power, riches, wisdom, strength, honor, glory, and blessing.
Then every creature in all creation joins in, praising both the Father on the throne and the Lamb forever.
The four creatures say “Amen,” and the elders fall down in worship. Heaven’s worship scene is complete.
